item.title: What does it mean to be an 'associate member' of the EU?
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen proposed an ‘Alliance for the Future’ that could make Canada the EU's first ‘associate member’. But what is an ‘associate member ’, and what does this alliance mean for the EU and Canada? Watch the video!

item.title: North Korea slams South's claim it was behind DMZ mine blasts, calling it a 'farce'
item.description: North Korea in recent years has added mines, anti-tank barriers and other front-line fortifications, raising concerns in the South about the growing presence of North Korean soldiers near the border.

item.title: ‘Europe is ending its addiction to a toxic, costly drug’: Heat pump sales soar as electricity taxes fall
item.description: Heat pump sales plummeted in 2024 – but now they’re on the rise again. Here’s why.

item.title: Majorca vs Menorca vs Ibiza: Which of Spain’s Balearic Islands should you visit?
item.description: They may be part of the same archipelago, but Majorca, Menorca and Ibiza each have their own distinct character. Here’s what to know before booking.

item.title: Albanian PM says fate of Kushner-linked luxury project will be decided by 'science', not 'ideology'
item.description: Albania has previously promised that the €1.4bn project linked to Donald Trump's son-in-law will meet EU environmental standards.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | September 30th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this September 30th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Diesel taxes in Europe: Which countries charge the most?
item.description: Diesel has overtaken petrol as Europe's most expensive fuel, at a record €2.226 per litre. Yet EU governments still tax it about 12 cents less than petrol.

item.title: Air pollution is slowing down marathon runners, study finds
item.description: Higher levels of nitrogen dioxide on race day are linked to slower marathon times, particularly among non-elite runners, new research suggests.

item.title: Morocco's King Mohammed VI appoints Fatima Mansouri as the country's first female prime minister
item.description: Mansouri is only the second woman in the Arab world to hold the office of prime minister. Her established political career has seen her serve as mayor of Marrakesh and member of parliament previously.

item.title: Top AI and tech firms sign 'morally binding' accord to 'self-police' development after meeting at White House
item.description: The accord comes amid massive global pressure from civilians and lawmakers alike to regulate the industry as reports of the technology breaking out of its confines continue to pile. Last week OpenAI revealed that its agent had hacked into an Australian government website during its testing phase.

item.title: A little known greenhouse gas is quietly harming half of Europeans. This Italian city is hit hardest
item.description: People who suffer from asthma are the most at risk.

item.title: Man City found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of financial rules, Premier League says
item.description: A statement from the English Premier League said an independent commission found that the club had arranged "sham" contracts and agreements to artificially inflate its revenues and reduce its costs.

item.title: Stellantis to halt four French plants for several days over supply shortage
item.description: The Italian-French-American carmaker has been hit by surging demand for electric vehicles, particularly from business customers.

item.title: Ukraine pushes for 'bold action' on Russian assets to plug $78 billion gap in 2027
item.description: Russia's relentless airstrikes are deepening Ukraine's financial gap. As costs rise and the deficit swells, the country is pleading with European allies to tap into the immobilised Russian assets.

item.title: No energy shortages, but a painful winter looms for Europe, top EU energy leader warns
item.description: Europe needs to protect consumers from another energy price shock while making fossil fuels less central to the economy. Emergency measures can soften the immediate blow, but Brussels is warning governments not to let short-term subsidies or tax decisions undermine the green transition.

item.title: Pressure grows within EPP to expel Vučić’s SNS party over Mladić funeral
item.description: The EU’s largest political family linked the participation of senior Serbian officials at Mladić’s funeral to its ongoing scrutiny of the Serbian Progressive Party, which could ultimately lead to its suspension or expulsion from the EPP.

item.title: With two Orbán-era ministers detained, Magyar's 'Operation Purge' takes shape
item.description: Prime Minister Péter Magyar’s “Operation Purge” has entered a new phase with the detention of two former ministers. Holding officials from the Orbán era to account was a central campaign pledge, and Magyar says the drive will now accelerate. Fidesz has denounced the effort as political revenge.

item.title: Spanish company Sateliot to launch five satellites with SpaceX to boost global 5G
item.description: Sateliot is launching five satellites with SpaceX on Thursday, taking its constellation to 11. The Draconis mission will double daily passes, halve revisit time and bolster its 5G NTN IoT connectivity service.

item.title: Euronews Travel & Tourism Summit 2026: Five of the key takeaways
item.description: Figures from across the travel industry joined Euronews in Brussels on 29 September. Here’s the most important things to know.

item.title: French students blockade schools nationwide to demand more resources
item.description: Hundreds of secondary school students blocked school entrances in Rennes and Paris during a national day of action, calling for more staff and funding for education.

item.title: Russian nuclear-capable Tu-95 crashes in Far East, killing six crew members
item.description: The bomber went down near Krasnoyarovo shortly after taking off from the Ukrainka air base, which Russia had used to shelter surviving strategic bombers after Ukraine's Operation Spiderweb destroyed or damaged more than 40 aircraft at Russian airfields in June 2025.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | September 29th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this September 29th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Baku Security Forum puts cross-border threats in focus
item.description: The Baku Security Forum brought together security and intelligence officials from different countries to discuss counterterrorism, emerging threats and stronger international cooperation.

item.title: UK PM Burnham to lay out 'options' for EU relations later this year
item.description: The country's divisive 2016 vote to leave the EU has once again been thrust under the spotlight this year amid mounting calls from leading Labour figures for Britain to re-enter the bloc.

item.title: Nvidia rival AMD bets $8.2bn on the 'godmother of AI' and her virtual worlds
item.description: World Labs builds world models, AI systems designed to understand how objects and spaces behave, allowing them to simulate what might happen when something moves or an action is taken.

item.title: Global economic impact of Iran war ‘unbearable,’ Qatar warns as talks continue
item.description: The war has choked shipping through Hormuz and disrupted Gulf exports. Qatar said it has continued to mediate between Washington and Tehran, warning that the fallout has now affected multiple sectors and not just energy.

item.title: Eiffel Tower director announces departure after row over sidelining of female staff
item.description: A month ago, the exclusion of female staff during a visit by an ultraconservative Hindu group sparked a strike and forced the monument to close for a day.

item.title: Tokyo records longest rainy streak on record with 34 consecutive days
item.description: Tokyo has recorded 34 consecutive days of rain, marking the longest such streak on record, according to Japan's weather agency.

item.title: France's public debt soars to a record 119% of GDP
item.description: France's public debt reached 3,595.5 billion euros at the end of June, Insee said, a record high that is set to keep rising as the outlook worsens.

item.title: IEA could consider more oil reserve releases as Europe faces tough winter
item.description: The IEA says it could consider releasing more emergency oil stocks if supply disruptions worsen, although another release is not currently its top priority. Europe faces a difficult winter after spending more than €100bn extra on energy imports since the Iran war began.

item.title: Azerbaijan Tourism Board CEO: Baku-Brussels flights on the horizon for 2027
item.description: Azerbaijan is boosting connectivity with four-weekly flights between Baku and Brussels. But beyond the capital, Azerbaijan Tourism Board CEO Florian Sengstschmid told Euronews that visitors should discover the country’s hidden villages.

item.title: Evicted 87-year-old Madrid pensioner can return home, says tenants union
item.description: An 87-year-old woman whose eviction fuelled protests over Spain’s housing crisis will be able to return to her Madrid home following an agreement with the property owner.

item.title: Spanish government unveils new measures aimed at easing housing crisis
item.description: The government has been facing growing pressure from a housing protest movement amid high costs and public outcry over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman.

item.title: Pope's visit to France is 'beginning of a new mission to Europe', expert says
item.description: Austen Ivereigh, a fellow in Contemporary Church History at Oxford University, thinks one of the biggest themes of Pope Leo XIV's pontificate will be "to build a new world order", as he sees the old one "has crumbled".

item.title: Middle East oil exports rise as LNG traffic through Hormuz picks up
item.description: Months into the war with Iran, Gulf exporters are finding ways to keep oil and gas moving, but crossing Hormuz remains risky and some customers are still missing contracted cargoes.

item.title: One in eight cancer cases worldwide is linked to preventable infections, study finds
item.description: Infections caused by viruses, bacterium and parasites caused an estimated 2.3 million new cancer cases in 2024, with low- and middle-income countries bearing most of the burden.

item.title: Counterfeit medicine trade: how online pharmacies are selling deadly fake painkillers across Europe
item.description: Deadly synthetic opioids disguised as legitimate painkillers are being sold online across Europe, as counterfeit medicines linked to multiple deaths in the Netherlands expose the dark side of e-commerce.

item.title: Masters of Uzbekistan: how traditional crafts are passed on to new generations
item.description: Traditional workshops in Uzbekistan are teaching younger generations the skills behind woodcarving, embroidery and ceramics, while adapting their work to contemporary tastes and new opportunities.

item.title: Protesters march for unrestricted abortion access in Chile and Colombia
item.description: Demonstrators gathered in Santiago and Bogotá on International Safe Abortion Day, calling for greater access to abortion and defending reproductive rights.

item.title: Italy's battery gold rush: Energy storage creates a new market
item.description: From paper projects to batteries now online: the energy market is changing and the value of storage is soaring worldwide

item.title: Celine Dion surprises Paris Fashion Week with performance at L'Oréal show
item.description: Canadian singer Celine Dion made a surprise appearance at L'Oréal's fashion show in Paris, performing on stage with the Eiffel Tower in the background alongside a star-studded line-up of celebrities and models.

item.title: Inflation in Spain surges to 4.9% in September on higher fuel prices
item.description: Inflation in Spain climbed 0.6% in September to 4.9%, driven by higher fuel prices, lubricants and package holidays. Core inflation rose 0.2% to 3.1%.

item.title: ‘KEEP OU-’: Banksy’s powerful anti-Brexit installation to go up for sale
item.description: Titled “Keep Ou T” and currently displayed ahead of Phillips' Frieze Week Modern & Contemporary Art Auctions in London, the artwork dates from 2019 and goes under the hammer next month.

item.title: Exclusive: EU-wide digital levy might generate up to €25bn annually for next budget
item.description: The European Parliament's proposed digital levy could raise up to €25bn a year for the next EU budget, five times the Commission's estimate, according to figures shared exclusively with Euronews by MEP Danuše Nerudová.

item.title: European Travel Commission CEO: 'Climate change is the biggest threat to tourism right now'
item.description: While Europe remains the world’s tourism playground, Eduardo Santander of the European Travel Commission told Euronews that the continent needs to coordinate better to tackle climate challenges and congestion.

item.title: Polo makes landfall in Mexico as Category 3 hurricane, cutting power and causing floods
item.description: This year's Pacific hurricane season is shaping up as more severe than usual, as a Super El Niño, an extreme version of a recurring weather pattern, wreaks devastation, in the form of historic droughts and flooding.

item.title: French students clash with police as blockades over conditions in schools intensify
item.description: Tens of thousands were expected to rally in Paris and other cities, with teachers and fire services striking nationwide although with public transport not badly affected.

item.title: ‘Climate change is very much related to travel costs,’ says tourism chief
item.description: European Travel Commission CEO Eduardo Santander says rising travel costs, labour shortages and climate change are putting pressure on Europe’s tourism industry.

item.title: Central Europe should be marketed as one destination, tourism leaders tell Euronews Travel & Tourism Summit
item.description: Hungarian and French tourism leaders say closer cross-border cooperation could create richer experiences for visitors, while better use of data and greater protection of nature are vital to the region’s future.

item.title: Euronews Travel & Tourism Summit: US envoy says Global Entry for Belgians could come by end of 2026
item.description: Bill White, Ambassador of the United States to Belgium, told Euronews that Belgian travellers could soon breeze through major US airports as Global Entry plans move forward.
